draft.title: Safe, connected and belonging
card: Liveability is how well a place meets the needs of the people who live there. Some of those needs are about feelings, not just buildings and services.
Safe
people who feel safe in their streets, homes and public spaces tend to rate their place as more liveable.
Included and connected
people who feel welcome and have family, friends or neighbours nearby tend to rate their place as more liveable. Clubs and shared events, such as local festivals, help people feel connected.
Belonging to a community is part of its identity. People who feel they belong rate a place higher. People who feel left out or threatened tend to rate the same place lower.
draft.remember: People rate a place higher when they feel safe, connected and that they belong, and lower when they feel left out or threatened.

a.q: Aroha, in Year 7, has just moved to a new town. Which change would most likely lead her to rate it as more liveable?
opts: She joins a local netball team and makes friends
She stops going to the park after being teased there
She feels unsafe walking home past an empty lot
She is left out of a group chat by her classmates
a.why: Joining a team helps her feel included and connected to others, and these feelings tend to raise how people rate a place. Being teased, feeling unsafe or being left out are also feelings, but they tend to lower her rating, not raise it.
a.clue: Does each change bring her closer to others or push her away?

b.q: Two families live on the same street in Bendigo. One rates it as highly liveable. The other rates it low. Which reason best explains the difference?
opts: The second family feels left out by its neighbours
The first family feels unwelcome at the local club
The second family has made many friends nearby
Both families feel safe walking along the street
b.why: Feeling left out tends to lower how people rate a place, so it explains why the second family rates the street low. Feeling unwelcome would lower the first family's rating, which is the wrong way round, and a feeling both families share cannot explain a difference.
b.clue: Which reason would lower one family's rating but not the other's?

a.best: She joins a local netball team and makes friends

b.best: The second family feels left out by its neighbours

proposal.title: Social connectedness and community identity
card: Liveability is how well a place meets the needs of the people who live there. Some of those needs are about feelings, not just buildings and services.
